open_points.subject: A10 effect approval lifecycle when approved request_digest no longer matches
open_points.text: A10 rule 1: "an approved, unused approval whose request_digest no longer matches ... stays approved and unused ... the kernel proceeds as if it did not exist"; A10 rule 3: "Approving sends the effect at once ... and the approval becomes used with the attempt's outcome".
open_points.question: When the owner approves a requested approval whose digest is now stale, does the kernel mark that approval `used` or keep it `approved` and unused, and does it send under grant immediately if a grant applies?
options: Keep stale approval `approved` and unused; if grant applies, send under grant in the same owner request
Always mark approved approval `used` on approve, even if stale, then either send or wait
Refuse deciding stale requested approvals instead of accepting them
open_points.default_guess: Keep stale approval `approved` and unused, and if a grant applies send under grant immediately.

open_points.subject: A11 authority check vs A10 resend-after-not_applied rule
open_points.text: A10 rule 1: "a resend after not_applied ... needs a fresh approval ... send is not ... under a standing grant"; A11 rule 1 authority order: "for a draft-write ... otherwise an approval or a grant".
open_points.question: After a `not_applied` resolution, can a grant authorize the next send, or is fresh approval mandatory with no grant path for all effect classes?
options: Fresh approval is mandatory; grants cannot authorize that resend
Grant may authorize resend for non-destructive classes
Grant may authorize resend except for draft-write
open_points.default_guess: Fresh approval is mandatory and grant cannot authorize the resend.

open_points.subject: A16 token-list re-read failure recovery loop
open_points.text: A16 rule 2: "when [file bytes hash] differ, or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it ..." and "When any fails, every request is refused ... until a re-read passes".
open_points.question: After one failed re-read (for example parse error), if the file later becomes readable with unchanged bytes hash, what forces another re-read so the system can leave refusal mode?
options: While in refusal mode, attempt re-read on every request regardless of hash equality
Only re-read on hash change; system can remain blocked indefinitely until file content changes
Require restart to clear refusal mode
open_points.default_guess: While in refusal mode, re-read on every request until one passes.

open_points.subject: A08 manifest JSON validity for duplicate member names
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 uses "record is not valid JSON"; A01 rule 1 says duplicate keys are refused "where it enters" for kernel-entered values, but no explicit rule states how duplicate keys in manifest files are treated.
open_points.question: If a manifest file or capability entry contains duplicate JSON member names, must proposal/invocation treat it as manifest mismatch, or accept parser-dependent behavior?
options: Treat duplicate member names as invalid JSON and refuse as manifest mismatch
Allow parser behavior (e.g., last-key-wins) and continue
Treat duplicates as a separate explicit manifest-mismatch reason
open_points.default_guess: Treat duplicate member names as invalid JSON and refuse as manifest mismatch.
